mainEntity.name: Do I need to live in Spain to buy a house in Valencia?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Non-residents can buy property in Valencia without becoming Spanish residents. You will need an NIE number and must comply with Spanish tax and anti-money-laundering requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long does buying a property in Valencia take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The time depends on the due diligence, the date the notary can offer and, if there is a mortgage, the bank’s approval and valuation. Your lawyer can set a timetable once the legal checks start.

mainEntity.name: Can I buy a property in Valencia remotely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With a power of attorney, your Spanish lawyer can handle the NIE application, contract signing, notary completion and post-completion formalities on your behalf.

mainEntity.name: What taxes do non-residents pay when buying in Valencia?

acceptedAnswer.text: For resale properties, buyers usually pay ITP transfer tax. For new builds, buyers usually pay VAT and stamp duty. Non-resident owners may also need to file Modelo 210 every year.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a Spanish bank account?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not always legally mandatory, but it is strongly recommended for paying taxes, utilities, community fees and annual property-related costs.
Modelo 210 is the Spanish non-resident income tax return. Non-resident property owners must file it whether the property is rented out or kept for personal use.

mainEntity.name: Can a UK citizen buy property in Valencia after Brexit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. UK citizens can still buy property in Spain after Brexit. The purchase process is broadly the same, although residence and immigration rights are separate matters.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I die without a Spanish will?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your home country’s succession law may apply, but the process can become slower and more complex. A Spanish will covering your Spanish assets is usually recommended. Our inheritance law team can assist with this.
